title: Couscous with Roasted Vegetables
subtitle: Fluffy couscous with roasted pepper, courgette and aubergine
excerpt: Plain couscous made fluffy with stock, topped with roasted red peppers, courgette and aubergine, dressed with lemon juice and olive oil. A substantial vegetable salad that eats as a full lunch.
sourceNotes: Couscous salads with roasted vegetables became a fixture of British salad bars and lunch menus in the late 1990s and early 2000s as couscous moved from specialist ingredient to supermarket staple. The combination of roasted Mediterranean vegetables with couscous draws on North African cooking traditions, adapted for the British cold-lunch context.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps for 2 days in the fridge. Best eaten at room temperature.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Roast the vegetables and make the couscous up to a day ahead; keep separately and assemble when needed.

content.text: Couscous with roasted vegetables is a reliable summer lunch. The couscous needs to be fluffy rather than clumped, which means using the right amount of liquid (just enough to absorb completely) and fluffing it thoroughly with a fork. The vegetables should be properly roasted rather than just softened: colour and slight caramelisation bring the flavour that makes this more than a side dish.

Heat the oven to 200 C. Spread the red peppers, courgette and aubergine on a large baking tray. Drizzle with {{olive-oil}} of olive oil and season with half the salt. Toss to coat. Roast for 25 to 30 minutes, turning halfway, until the vegetables are tender and coloured at the edges.

Put {{couscous}} of couscous in a large bowl. Pour over {{stock-vegetable}} of hot stock and the remaining salt. Stir once, cover with a plate and leave for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork to separate the grains.

Add the roasted vegetables to the couscous. Drizzle over the lemon juice and the remaining olive oil. Add the chopped parsley and {{black-pepper}} of black pepper. Toss everything together. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.cause: Not enough liquid or not fluffed properly.
items.fix: Use exactly 1.2 times the volume of stock to couscous. Fluff thoroughly with a fork, not a spoon.
Use two trays if needed. Vegetables need space to roast, not steam. The oven temperature of 200 C is important; lower and they stew.

content.text: Roasted vegetable couscous arrived in British home cooking via the salad bar culture of the 1990s, following routes opened by North African cookery writers and the growing interest in Middle Eastern food. It became practical once couscous was stocked in every supermarket. The method is simple and the result is filling: it makes a full lunch and travels well.
